Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

the arts building will keep the delivery sheet in the red desk after the driver leaves and dev will place any photographs in the shared ceramics folder before closing time mara wants the picture files to include the carton label and the damaged area in the same frame when possible if a label cannot be seen without moving a carton dev should photograph the damage first and write down the label instead of lifting the carton the class teacher expects to arrive at one thirty and needs the west room clear enough to set out her sample tiles the cleaning crew comes after six and will not enter the west room if the small sign is still on the crate so mara will remove it after she has checked the delivery the final count the temperature reading and the driver signature should all remain on the same sheet", "output": "We are handling the ceramics delivery for the north room at the Bellweather Community Arts Building, and I am forwarding the revised delivery sheet to Mara Voss at the front desk before the truck leaves the depot. The order comes from the Alder Creek Pottery Cooperative and includes forty-eight dinner plates, twenty-four shallow bowls, twelve serving platters, and six blue-glazed water pitchers. The pottery packed the pieces in nine cartons and one narrow crate. The crate holds the pitchers upright and has a red paper label on both short sides. The plates and bowls are in cartons marked with a white moon; the platters are in cartons marked with a green square. The driver is Lewis Grant, and his truck number is thirty-seven. The delivery window on the sheet is from nine thirty to ten fifteen on Thursday, May 4.

The road into the Arts Building has a low stone arch, and the truck cannot pass beneath it. The driver needs to stop at the gravel lay-by beside the old pump house, then roll the cartons through the west service entrance on hand carts. Mara told me the entrance door sticks if the outside temperature is below eight degrees, and she has put a rubber wedge in the blue supply cabinet for that reason. The route from the lay-by crosses a tiled courtyard with a shallow drain near the fountain. There is a temporary board over the drain, but the board shifts when a cart wheel catches its edge. The building caretaker says the board will be secured before the delivery arrives. The caretaker also asked us to keep the loading area clear for a piano tuner who is expected at eleven.

The pottery asked for a signature at delivery and a count of every carton before the driver leaves. Mara will sign the delivery sheet, but she will not sign the damage form unless she has checked the pieces herself. She has arranged for Dev Patel from the studio to be there with a clipboard and a small flashlight. Dev will inspect the outer packing and record dents or wet patches without opening a carton. The pottery said that any broken glaze or chipped rim should be photographed beside the carton label and reported to its office by the end of the day. Mara said, “If anything arrives damp, leave the paper around it until I can look at the carton.” No one should use the tall shelves beside the kiln because the lower brackets are loose, and the shelves are being repaired next week.

The room is prepared for the delivery, but the tables are not all in the same place. The folding table near the sink is reserved for the pitchers, and the long maple table is for the platters. The plates should stay on their original cartons until the class teacher comes in the afternoon. She wants to check the glaze colors against two sample tiles. The sample tiles are in a padded envelope inside the locked drawer of the red desk. The key is with Mara, and the drawer sometimes catches when it is pulled straight out. Dev knows to lift the handle slightly before opening it. There are four blue cotton pads in the red desk for the pitchers and two rolls of brown paper under the maple table. No one has ordered packing foam for this delivery.

Section Three: The count to use when the truck is at the entrance.
1. The first count is nine cartons and one narrow crate.
2. The second count is forty-eight plates, twenty-four bowls, twelve platters, and six pitchers.
3. The third check is that the red labels stay on the short sides of the crate and the white moon and green square remain readable on the cartons.

Mara wants the carton count written in the left margin of the delivery sheet. The piece count goes in the box marked “contents,” and the time the last item enters the building goes in the box marked “received at.” Dev should note whether the blue cabinet wedge was used and whether the courtyard board stayed in place. These are separate observations, and he should not combine them into one comment.

The forecast on the wall calendar shows light rain around noon, but the delivery is scheduled before that. The canopy above the west entrance is narrow, and water runs from its left corner after a long shower. Mara asked the caretaker to place a dry runner inside the door rather than across the courtyard. The runner has a dark rubber backing and a paper tag that says “west entrance only.” The spare runner in the closet is cream-colored and belongs to the gallery. If rain begins early, the driver can wait under the canopy while Dev checks the cartons. The pottery office number is printed at the bottom of the delivery sheet, and Mara has written the studio extension beside it. The office closes at four thirty and does not monitor messages on Sunday.

The driver called this morning to ask whether he should bring the empty hand carts back to the depot. Mara said the Arts Building has two carts of its own, and the driver may take his carts away after unloading. She also asked him to leave the narrow crate beside the folding table instead of putting it under the table because the crate has a fragile base. The delivery sheet lists a wooden brace inside the crate, but the brace is only for transport and should stay with the crate if the pottery collects it later. Lewis said, “I will keep the crate upright and leave the brace where it is until someone from the cooperative gives me a collection date.” Dev will put a small sign on the crate so the evening cleaning crew does not move it.

If the kiln room temperature is above twenty-four degrees when the pottery arrives, the cartons must remain sealed in the west room until the class teacher can move them to the cooler cabinet. If the temperature is twenty-four degrees or lower, the cartons may be opened after Dev has recorded the labels and Mara has signed the count. Dev will read the wall thermometer before anyone opens a carton and write the number beside the received time. This condition matters because the blue glaze can soften when it warms too quickly. Mara has not asked anyone to change the kiln setting, and the caretaker has not promised that the room will be cool. The thermometer was checked last Monday, and the caretaker plans to check it again on Thursday morning.

The Arts Building will keep the delivery sheet in the red desk after the driver leaves, and Dev will place any photographs in the shared ceramics folder before closing time. Mara wants the picture files to include the carton label and the damaged area in the same frame when possible. If a label cannot be seen without moving a carton, Dev should photograph the damage first and write down the label instead of lifting the carton. The class teacher expects to arrive at one thirty and needs the west room clear enough to set out her sample tiles. The cleaning crew comes after six and will not enter the west room if the small sign is still on the crate, so Mara will remove it after she has checked the delivery. The final count, the temperature reading, and the driver signature should all remain on the same sheet."}]
